Subject: Follow-up: Acme Cloud discovery - incident response and next tests

Hi Alice - thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and suggested next steps from our discovery call:

Summary of what we heard:
- You run a customer-facing inference API that must meet 99.95% availability and sub-200ms 95th percentile tail for small requests.
- Primary concern: how different inference vendors handle P1/P2 incidents, RCA timelines, and whether there are automatic fallbacks to alternate model variants/regions.
- You're evaluating Redwood vs. hyperscalers (AWS/GCP) and one other inference API vendor (VentureTech).

Redwood next steps (proposed):
1) Send a short SLA/incident-response comparison matrix for Redwood vs. the hyperscalers + VentureTech (we'll include response times, escalation path, RCA commitments).
2) Provide a sanitized sample incident log (500 lines) and our typical RCA template so you can judge the level of detail.
3) Run a short incident-recovery drill next week (we can simulate a P1 degraded KV cache scenario) - 30 minute window, Redwood ops + Acme SRE on call.
4) Align on procurement / commercial timeline (we noted you target a decision by end of July).

Can you confirm the team who should join the drill? I think you mentioned Bill Turner (SRE) and maybe your security lead.

I'll attach the SLA matrix and sample incident log in my next email.

Best,
Jonas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Jonas - thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Yes, Bill will join the drill but our security lead (sarah.sec@acmecloud.com) should also be looped for the RCA template review.
- For hyperscaler comparisons, we care less about advertised SLA and more about historical incident cadence and the depth of post-incident RCAs (we've seen generic "root cause" notes without actionable mitigation in the past).
- Two specific asks: 1) Can you confirm P1 acknowledgement + initial mitigation contact times? 2) What is your policy for sharing raw traces/logs for customers during an RCA (do you redact or provide full access)?

Also can you include any examples of escalation times when you've had to route traffic to alternate regions/models?

alice@acmecloud.com

Alice - answers inline and attaching the matrix + sample log.

> 1) P1 acknowledgement + initial mitigation contact times?
- For Redwood Dedicated and Private customers we commit to a P1 initial response < 15 minutes (phone + PagerDuty). For Hosted customers our SRE team targets < 30 minutes for initial response and we offer accelerated 15-minute response as an add-on SLA.

> 2) Policy for sharing raw traces/logs for customers?
- We provide sanitized traces and relevant request/response logs with timestamps and correlation ids by default. For Dedicated/Private we can provide more complete raw logs under an NDA and accepted data handling agreement.

> Examples of routing to alternate regions/models?
- We have two recent incidents: in March 2026 we auto-failed traffic to a secondary region when a networking issue impacted a set of GPU hosts (customer-facing failover, 6-minute cutover). In May 2026 we performed model-variant fallback for customers on constrained hardware where quantized model degraded; we served from a compatibility variant with a 1.2x latency increase but zero customer-visible errors while the primary pool recovered.

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-sla-matrix.pdf, acme-incident-log-sample.csv

Next steps:
- Let's schedule the incident drill on Tue 2026-07-21 10:00 PT (30 min). Does that work for Bill and Sarah?
- I'll ask Rishi to outline our formal RCA timeline and what we include in a customer RCA (timeline, root cause analysis, mitigations, corrective action plan).

Jonas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: acme-incident-log-sample.csv (CSV, 42KB)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Acme Cloud discovery - incident response & RCA expectations

Hi Alice - quick note on RCA commitments and timeline from an SRE perspective.

What we include in a customer RCA:
- Executive summary with impact window and customer-facing timeline.
- Detailed technical timeline (system metrics, RPC traces, KV cache state, autoscaler events).
- Root cause analysis with supporting evidence (stack traces, config drift, kernel-level issues if applicable).
- Short-term mitigations performed and long-term corrective actions (code fixes, configuration changes, runbook updates).
- Postmortem owner and estimated ETA for each corrective action.

Timeline commitments:
- Initial incident acknowledgement: P1 < 15m (Dedicated/Private), P1 < 30m (Hosted standard).
- Customer-facing preliminary incident summary: within 8 hours of incident closure.
- Full RCA draft: within 5 business days for high-severity incidents; finalized RCA within 10 business days after internal review.

Logs and traces:
- We will provide sanitized traces and correlation IDs by default. For customers with a signed data access addendum we can provide redacted raw traces. For regulated customers we can arrange a secure session to review raw traces under an NDA.

If you'd like a copy of a redacted RCA from a comparable incident (with identifying data removed), we can share that as well.

Also confirming: the drill proposed for 2026-07-21 10:00 PT works for our ops team - we will provide a short playbook in advance.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Reliability | Redwood Inference
